subtopics.title: Soil: The Living Skin That Feeds the Country

questions.question: Soil is treated as a non-renewable resource because:
options: A few centimetres of topsoil take centuries to form under African conditions, while a single storm on bare ground can strip more than that in an afternoon
It contains minerals that never regenerate
It cannot be transported between farms
Parent rock is scarce in South Africa

questions.question: Nearly all soil fertility lives in:
options: The parent rock at depth
The dark, humus-rich topsoil, whose humus stores nutrients and moisture and binds particles into stable crumbs
The subsoil's clay layers
The water table

questions.question: South Africa's arable endowment is approximately:
options: Half the country arable, a quarter high-potential
30% arable, 15% high-potential
12% arable, with barely 3% truly high-potential land
2% arable in total

questions.question: Vegetation is called the soil's bodyguard because:
options: It shades the soil from sunlight damage
It attracts rainfall to the area
It keeps animals away from fields
Leaves break the force of falling rain, roots bind the crumbs, and litter feeds the humus that holds soil together

subtopics.title: Causes of Soil Erosion: Human, Animal and Physical

questions.question: The escalating sequence of water erosion is:
options: Splash, sheet, rill, then gully — dongas being the end state
Gully, rill, sheet, splash
Sheet, splash, gully, rill
Splash, gully, sheet, rill

questions.question: The examiner's nuance about physical causes is that:
options: They operate only in deserts
Physical agents mostly finish what land use starts — bare ground is the precondition, and bare ground is usually made
They are stronger than all human causes combined
They ceased after the Dust Bowl

questions.question: The past human cause whose scars remain in the Eastern Cape's dongas is:
options: The 1930s American Dust Bowl
Colonial railway construction
Apartheid's homeland system concentrating too many people and animals on too little land, forcing overuse
Early irrigation schemes

questions.question: Trampling by cattle contributes to erosion because:
options: Hooves fertilise the soil excessively
Cattle eat the soil directly
Trampled paths attract wind erosion only
Compacted paths stop water soaking in, so it runs off — cattle tracks to water points often become the starter channels for gullies

subtopics.title: Evidence and Effects Across South Africa

questions.question: The textbook South African case of dam siltation is:
options: The Welbedacht Dam on the Caledon River, which lost most of its capacity within decades of construction
The Gariep Dam doubling its capacity
The Vaal Dam silting completely by 1950
Katse Dam in Lesotho overflowing

questions.question: A river running brown after a storm is evidence of erosion because:
options: Brown indicates algae growth
The colour is topsoil in transit — fertile land washing toward the sea
It shows the river is flooding
Brown water means acid mine drainage

questions.question: An effect of erosion on people, distinct from environmental effects, is:
options: Wetlands choking with sediment
Reduced veld biodiversity
Falling yields and shrinking farm incomes, rising food prices, collapsing rural livelihoods and costly fertiliser substituting for lost fertility
Sharper flood peaks in rivers

questions.question: Erosion is called a slow-motion disaster because:
options: It occurs only over geological time
It affects slow-growing crops most
Storms move slowly across the country
No single storm makes headlines, but the cumulative loss undermines food security, water security and rural livelihoods simultaneously

subtopics.title: Management, and the GIS Toolkit for Soil

questions.question: Contour ploughing prevents erosion because:
options: Furrows run along the slope's contours, so each ridge dams runoff instead of channelling it downhill
It turns the soil more deeply than normal ploughing
It removes the need for fallow periods
It increases the field's slope

questions.question: Gabions control existing gullies by:
options: Draining water away faster
Acting as rock-packed wire barriers across the channel that slow water and trap sediment, letting the gully floor rise and re-vegetate
Poisoning invasive plants
Diverting rivers around the donga

questions.question: Spatial resolution and spectral resolution refer respectively to:
options: Map scale and map projection
Point data and area data
The ground size of one pixel, and which wavelength bands the sensor records — infrared exposing bare or stressed ground
The satellite's height and speed

questions.question: In a GIS, a borehole, a river and a catchment are stored respectively as:
options: Line, point and area data
Area, line and point data
Point, area and line data
Point, line and area (polygon) data

subtopics.title: The Bank Account That Fills by Teaspoons

questions.question: 'Deposits by teaspoon, withdrawals by bucket' summarises:
options: Soil forming over centuries while one storm on bare ground can remove decades of accumulation
The cost of fertiliser against the cost of seed
Rainfall variability in South Africa
The difference between topsoil and subsoil

questions.question: The 'one plate in ten' picture describes:
options: South Africa's food import ratio
Only about one-tenth of South Africa's land being arable, with a sliver of that high-potential — the plate sixty million people eat from
The share of farmland under irrigation
The portion of harvest lost to pests

questions.question: 'Every cause of erosion becomes one story: something fired the bodyguard' means:
options: Erosion is caused mainly by police absence
Farm security prevents erosion
Nearly every cause works by removing the protective vegetation whose leaves, roots and litter defend the soil
Animals guard soil better than plants

subtopics.title: How a Footpath Becomes a Canyon

questions.question: The five acts of the donga plot, in order, are:
options: Overgrazing bares a patch; raindrops splash soil loose; sheetwash steals the surface; rills form; rills join and deepen into a donga
Donga; rills; sheetwash; splash; bare patch
Splash; donga; overgrazing; rills; sheetwash
Sheetwash; splash; overgrazing; donga; rills

questions.question: Many dongas 'begin life as a footpath' because:
options: Footpaths are dug below ground level
Daily trampling compacts the path hard so water cannot soak in, making it the first drain that concentrates runoff
Paths are always on the steepest slopes
Walkers carry soil away on their shoes

questions.question: Wind erosion 'lifts the fine, fertile grains first', which matters because:
options: Coarse sand is more valuable
Fine grains cause dust allergies
The soil left behind is the infertile coarse fraction — the field keeps its bulk but loses its fertility, as the Dust Bowl showed
Wind only blows in deserts

questions.question: History enters South Africa's erosion plot because:
options: Erosion began only after 1994
Colonial farmers introduced gabions
The Dust Bowl occurred in the Karoo
Apartheid crowded people and cattle onto the smallest, poorest land, building overuse into the map — hence the deepest dongas in former homeland districts

questions.question: The 'winter blanket' for fields between seasons is:
options: Mulch, stubble and cover crops keeping the ground from ever lying bare
Plastic sheeting over the topsoil
A layer of imported sand
Flooding the fields shallowly

questions.question: Gabions work like 'speed bumps' because:
options: They stop cattle crossing the donga
Each storm's water stumbles over them, drops its load of soil, and the canyon floor slowly rises until grass can hold it
They redirect water onto the road
They pump water back upslope

questions.question: Running 'only as many animals as the grass can feed' applies the concept of:
options: Strip cropping
Spectral resolution
The veld's carrying capacity, combined with rotational resting of camps
Crop rotation

questions.question: Bare ground 'betrays itself from orbit' because:
options: Satellites photograph individual furrows
Bare soil is always lighter in colour
Soil emits radio signals when dry
Healthy vegetation reflects infrared strongly, so infrared bands reveal bare or stressed ground — spectral resolution at work
